interview.question: Decide all eight recommendations independently using attributable redacted evidence, never one shared outcome. For Azure VM DR, reconcile complete eligible VM/application/dependency populations, Azure-to-Azure Site Recovery and native backup configuration with separately approved RPO/RTO, recovery points, retention, network/failback and actual drill/restore evidence. For redundancy, preserve the immutable GRS-default wording but qualify Recovery Services versus Data Protection Backup vaults, datastore/workload/region support and Azure Files snapshot versus vaulted backup; generic account SKU and omitted settings prove no default or suitable backup choice. For guest deployment, distinguish legacy Guest Configuration wording from current Machine Configuration, direct versus Policy-created assignments, Audit/apply/autocorrect modes, exact guest extension publisher/type/instance names, identity/network/content prerequisites and current OS/architecture/VMSS/Arc support, including November 2026 Linux PowerShell changes; assignments do not prove execution or compliance. For security drift monitoring, separately substantiate expected baselines, Policy definitions/versions/assignments/parameters/exclusions, timely compliance observations, responsible review and operating response. No built-in fetch or second rule interpreter. For PaaS DR, assess every actual service/SKU/region and component/workload failover/failback plan with original-time drills; a SQL Database failover group is narrow configuration, not universal support, successful failover or achieved RPO/RTO. For native/third-party backup, substantiate compatible workload/version coverage, retention/restore/security and ownership; legacy Backup Center now points to Resiliency/Business Continuity Center, whose presence is not protection. For WAF diagnostics, bind the actual delivery resource/service to explicit enabled firewall-log categories and destinations, then independently substantiate ingestion, retention, regular attack and false-positive review/tuning. Standard/Premium Front Door uses FrontDoorWebApplicationFirewallLog; classic capitalization differs and is unsupported by this preparatory target model. The Sentinel walkthrough's FrontDoorFirewallLog names conflict with the service-specific monitoring page: do not equate them. For WAF-to-Sentinel, separately prove connector/content configuration, arriving WAF data, analytics/detection coverage and accountable response; shared workspace/onboarding and categories do not prove integration. All requirements, coverage, testing, operating decisions and exceptions remain blank until explicitly supplied. No live probes, commands, backup/restore/failover, guest or compliance execution, WAF attacks, queries, traffic or telemetry retrieval; no logs, guest/package/report payloads, scripts, settings, secrets, private endpoints or personal data retained.
